title: Richmond from Miller's Barn
summary: Madison County’s seat moved from hillside Milford to Col. John Miller’s land in 1798, where trustees named the new town Richmond for Miller’s birthplace.
bodyMarkdown:
Richmond, the seat of Madison County, grew from the farm of a Revolutionary War veteran. A fight over where the county court should sit gave the town its start in 1798. Today it is one of Kentucky's larger cities and home to Eastern Kentucky University.

## Before the town

The [Grokipedia article on Richmond](https://grokipedia.com/page/Richmond,_Kentucky) places the area's early history beside Fort Boonesborough, founded by Daniel Boone's party on April 1, 1775, on the Kentucky River about 10 miles from the future city. Madison County was formed from Lincoln County on August 22, 1786, and named for the Virginia statesman James Madison. Early settlers included Revolutionary War veterans and land speculators drawn to the Bluegrass soils and streams such as Otter Creek.

Colonel John Miller, a Yorktown veteran from Richmond, Virginia, acquired about 1,000 acres in the county around 1784. Grokipedia says he built a home and barn there that helped draw more settlers.

## Moving the county seat

The county's first seat was at Milford. The [Wikipedia article on Richmond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richmond,_Kentucky) says Miller successfully lobbied the Kentucky legislature to move it to his land. Milford's residents strongly opposed the change, but the county approved the transfer in March 1798.

Grokipedia says Miller donated 30 acres of his property for the new seat. It credits the choice to the site's central location, a noted spring and Miller's influence. On July 4, 1798, the new town was named Richmond in honor of Miller's Virginia birthplace. It was incorporated in 1809.

## The Battle of Richmond

Richmond's best-known event came during the Civil War. Confederate forces under Edmund Kirby Smith defeated Union troops under William Nelson near the town in late August 1862, as part of the Confederate invasion of Kentucky. Grokipedia dates the battle to August 29–30 and says the Confederates captured about 4,000 prisoners. Wikipedia gives August 30 and says Smith captured or killed 5,300 of Nelson's 6,500 men.

Wikipedia quotes one historian who called the battle "the nearest thing to a Cannae ever scored by any general, North or South." Grokipedia notes that the fighting crossed Madison County farmland and deepened divided loyalties among residents, who served on both sides.

## Growth

Grokipedia says the city reached 12,168 people by 1960. Highways, including Interstate 75, improved access to Lexington and beyond in the 1960s. Eastern Kentucky University was founded in 1906 as the Eastern Kentucky State Normal School and became a university in 1966, and it remains central to the local economy.

## Kentucky today

Richmond had 34,585 residents in the 2020 census, which Wikipedia says made it Kentucky's seventh-largest city. It remains the Madison County seat. Its founding connects to the Boonesborough settlement led by figures such as [Richard Callaway](/stories/col-richard-callaway-of-boonesborough/), and to the land company of [Richard Henderson](/stories/richard-henderson/).
